newsitem.title: USA: Egypt seen tendering for 500,000 tonnes of wheat.
newsitem.headline: Egypt seen tendering for 500,000 tonnes of wheat.

text.p: Talk was widespread talk in U.S. grain markets on Thursday that Egypt may tender for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat as early as next week for February/March shipment, U.S. exporters said.
Several exporters said they could not confirm the Egyptian tender but they did not rule out the possibility.
But they said they anticipated the wheat to be optional origin with very little business going to the United States.
"Our agent in Egypt said he expects a tender but he did not say when it would occur," one U.S. exporter said.

"I would expect it (the tender) to be 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat," the exporter said. He said they will probably issue an announcement for 50,000 tonnes, but would likely buy up to 500,000 tonnes.
The wheat could be from Australia, Argentina or the U.S. The shipment date was slated for February and maybe, for a part of March, the exporter said.
A second U.S. exporter said he has not seen anything from his agents but also noted the tender was possible.
"It would be logical for Egypt to be tendering," he said, adding that the U.S. could get a cargo of about 50,000 tonnes.

But one U.S. grain dealer said active grain shipping programs were underway in Argentina, Australia and Canada, limiting the amount of wheat those countries can sell to Egypt, if it needs it in February and March.
An Egyptian embassy spokesman in Washington D.C. was not aware of the tender.
"I cannot confirm the rumor," the embassy spokesman said.
